title: Terraform module: unified KMS/HSM flavors + Vault/SecretsManager bridge
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that abstracts 'KMS flavors' (AWS KMS, AWS CloudHSM-backed keys, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and provides an optional bridge to either HashiCorp Vault or cloud Secrets Manager. The goal is to let Private (VPC) deployments pick a KMS flavor via a single input variable, support HSM-backed key material for compliance customers, and optionally provision a secure vault->cloud secrets synchronization path for workloads that need both Vault and cloud-native secrets APIs.
implementation_notes: Module will expose a 'kms_flavor' enum variable: 'aws-kms', 'aws-cloudhsm', 'gcp-kms', 'azure-kv'
Provide submodules for each provider with consistent outputs (key_arn/key_id, kms_key_id, key_uri, kms_provider) to simplify consumption by private-deploy bootstrap and runtime modules

Add optional 'vault_bridge' block that creates short-lived transit keys or uses existing KMS keys to seal Vault auto-unseal + a one-way sync job (lambda/k8s job) that copies secrets into Secrets Manager when enabled
Support aliasing and rotation policy inputs: rotation_schedule_days, rotation_window, rotate_via_kms_api_or_vault
IAM/principal bindings should follow least-privilege patterns; module will output roles/policies that downstream can attach to service accounts/users
HSM path will validate CloudHSM cluster state (for AWS) and fail fast if nodes not healthy; provide ttl-based retries and clear error messages
Include a 'health_check' optional resource that provisions a lightweight monitor (CloudWatch or Prometheus exporter) to assert encrypt/decrypt roundtrip and vault auto-unseal connectivity
Implement acceptance tests with Terratest and a small ephemeral environment in CI that runs encrypt/decrypt, vault unseal, and secret sync dry-run
Follow Terraform Registry naming: redwoodk8s/kms-flavors/aws? (internal private registry), semantic versioning and changelog in module repo
Module must be idempotent for upgrade paths and include migration helpers (see migration_plan)
acceptance_criteria: Module can provision KMS key for each supported flavor with consistent output keys
Vault auto-unseal works against the provisioned KMS/HSM keys (or an existing key passed in)
Optional vault_bridge can be toggled on/off without destroying unrelated resources and performs a successful dry-run sync
Health check resource reports healthy when encrypt/decrypt roundtrip and vault unseal succeed
CI Terratest suite passes in PRs and nightly runs that cover each provider flavor
Documentation includes example usage for private deployment bootstrap and upgrade notes
testing_plan: Unit tests for Terraform with checkov and tflint
Integration tests using Terratest that spin up minimal infra in AWS and GCP test accounts
Canary run in staging private-deploy cluster (non-production) with vault_bridge=false to validate outputs
Chaos test for KMS key rotation: rotate via API and assert Vault re-unseal and service decrypts
Security review and penetration checklist to be run by SecOps before release
migration_plan: Provide migration module 'kms_flavor_migrate' that maps existing key resources to new module outputs
Step 1: Import existing KMS keys into Terraform state using documented import steps
Step 2: Run a dry-run to ensure no diffs for critical resources (IAM roles, KMS keys)
Step 3: Enable 'vault_bridge' in staging and run sync job in dry-run; validate secrets mapping
Step 4: Schedule a maintenance window for rotation that requires rekeying HSM-backed keys (if applicable)
Step 5: Post-migration verification: run 72-hour monitoring window checking decrypt success and Vault seal state
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Misconfigured IAM grants could expose key material. Mitigation: module emits least-privilege examples and CI checks for overly-broad policies
Risk: HSM cluster provisioning failures introduce long lead times. Mitigation: pre-provision CloudHSM clusters via infra runbook and add explicit pre-checks in module
Risk: Sync bridge could leak secrets if misconfigured. Mitigation: sync defaults to dry-run and requires explicit enable flag and audit logging
Risk: Upgrades may attempt to recreate keys. Mitigation: migration helpers + import guidance and guarded resource rename mappings
